spec_family.name: Interior Stair System Repaint (Combined Riser/Stringer + Railing)
spec_family.description: Combined prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted interior stair systems in occupied residential homes. Consolidates two NC specs (SF_STAIR_RISER_NC with 30 tasks + SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC with 43 tasks = 73 NC tasks) into a single RP spec with 69 tasks. Covers condition assessment (visual scan, adhesion test, coating ID, anti-slip verification), RP-specific prep (degloss, scrape/feather for failing paint, contamination treatment, caulk assess/replace), state-driven primer selection (adhesion, stain-block, mildew-resistant), fine-finish coat application (brush or spray) on 6 paintable items (risers EA, stringers LF, balusters EA, newels EA, handrails LF, base rails LF), interstage inspection/sanding between every coat, tread walkability verification throughout work, and customer walkthrough. Sixth interior RP spec.

includes: Condition assessment (visual scan with work light, ASTM D3359 adhesion test, coating identification latex vs oil, anti-slip verification of tread protection)
EPA Lead-Safe RRP evaluation and containment for pre-1978 homes (stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint -- historically oil-based, multi-layer from multiple repaints)
Surface contamination treatment (TSP wash for mildew, smoke, water stain, grease -- especially handrails with hand-oil buildup)
Mildew/biocide treatment for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE (rare on stairs but possible in basement stairwells)
Deglossing existing paint surfaces per component type (chemical or mechanical, canonical sequence)
Scraping loose and failing paint with contour scrapers for profiled components (turned balusters, newel detail, handrail profiles)
Feather-sanding all scraped edges (mandatory at all QT -- non-negotiable for fine finish)
Caulk assessment and replacement at stringer-to-wall, riser-to-stringer, and newel junction joints (partial, not full re-caulk)
State-driven primer selection and application (adhesion primer for failing/peeling, stain-block for smoke, mildew-resistant for moisture)
Spot priming all scraped/repaired areas to prevent flashing
Fine-finish coat application -- 2 coats QT3-QT4, 3 coats QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3 (brush or spray)
Interstage inspection, sanding (QT3 spot 220, QT4 full 220, QT5 thorough 220-320), and defect repair between every coat
Tread protection (Ram Board Stair Armor) -- FIRST task, maintained walkable throughout, daily verification in occupied home context
Floor protection at landings (canvas drop cloths -- RP always has finished floors)
Wall masking along stringer edge and railing area (spray method -- finished walls in RP context)
Spray containment for balusters (cardboard shields, HVLP preferred over airless per doctrine 6.3)
Carpet runner protection if present (RP-specific -- rosin paper with low-tack tape)
Wet paint safety signage at top and bottom of stairway (RP occupied home context)
Handrail bracket removal/reinstall at QT4+ (paint behind attachment points)
Handrail feel test at QT5 (glass-smooth standard -- run hand along entire length)
Optional polyurethane topcoat on handrails at QT5 (maximum hand-oil resistance)
Final inspection and touch-up across all components
Customer walkthrough (RP-specific -- occupied home context, ~10-15 min per stairway system)

excludes.item: Stair treads (floor-rated coating, painted absolutely last per doctrine)
Structural stair repair (broken treads, loose newels, damaged stringers)

excludes.route_to: Plumber/contractor -- moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting (gate condition)

excludes.item: Wall stringers handled by wall spec context
excludes.route_to: Covered when stringer is integral to wall surface -- not a separate paintable item

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling coat count, inspection rigor, interstage sanding discipline, defect tolerance, bracket removal, feel test, and poly topcoat. QT3 is MINIMUM for stairs -- no QT2 available.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=1.0x baseline (minimum for stairs). QT4=1.3x (global modifier, bracket removal, systematic inspection). QT5=1.5x + 3rd brush coat per FFD 15.10.3, feel test, optional poly topcoat. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique. Brush is default for stair detail work. Spray for production work (20+ balusters).
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush: default for RP (occupied, detail work). HVLP spray preferred over airless for in-place baluster work per doctrine 6.3. Spray break-even at ~20-25 balusters. In occupied RP homes, brush is even more dominant due to containment difficulty. spray_backroll and roll are NOT valid for stairs.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish coating sheen level. Semi-gloss is default for stairs (scuff/hand-oil resistance).
configuration_dimensions.notes: Satin at QT3+. Semi-gloss at QT4+ (default). Gloss at QT5 only. Flat/matte/eggshell NOT valid for stairs per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine.

configuration_dimensions.description: Universal 3-level condition scale driving prep intensity. Maps from substrate state assessment.
configuration_dimensions.notes: GOOD=SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep, skip prime if adhesion passes). FAIR=SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT or SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE (1.5x prep, scrape/feather + state-driven prime). POOR=SS_INT_PEELING or SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE (2.0x prep, full remediation + state-driven prime).

configuration_dimensions.description: Interior substrate state driving primer selection and prep pathway. Different stair components may have different states.
configuration_dimensions.notes: All 5 SS_INT_* states accepted. Each drives distinct prep pathway and primer selection. Worst state at system drives condition_scale.

configuration_dimensions.description: Baluster profile type driving production rate variation on baluster-specific tasks.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Square=1.0x baseline. Turned=1.75x per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 9.2. Applies to degloss, scrape/feather, prime, brush finish baluster tasks. Does NOT apply to spray finish (profile-independent spray rates).

configuration_dimensions.description: Stringer type driving production rate variation on stringer-specific tasks.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Closed=1.0x baseline. Open=1.4x (notched profile, more surface area). Applies to all stringer tasks.

paintable_items.name: Stair Riser Face
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count of stair risers to be repainted. One riser = one face (~2.2 SF per EA). Counted per individual riser.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Same physical item in RP context. Flat vertical surface -- efficient to degloss and paint.

paintable_items.name: Stair Stringer / Skirtboard
paintable_items.counting_rules: Linear feet of stringer/skirtboard to be repainted. Full diagonal run from bottom to top. Count each stringer separately.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. Open vs closed affects production rate (1.0x vs 1.4x). Stairwell access modifiers apply to stringer tasks.

paintable_items.name: Stair Baluster
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count of balusters to be repainted. Includes wood and iron balusters. Typical residential: 39-62 per stairway system.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC. DOMINANT cost driver. Profile type (square vs turned) is primary rate modifier. 62 turned balusters at 7 min/EA x 3 coats = ~22 hours of baluster painting alone.

paintable_items.name: Stair Newel Post
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count of newel posts to be repainted. All newels are wood regardless of baluster material. Typical: 2-4 per stairway system.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC. Larger surface area with decorative detail (caps, rosettes, flutes). ~4-8 SF per EA.

paintable_items.name: Stair Handrail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Linear feet of handrail to be repainted. Measured along handrail centerline. 4 surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside).
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC. Most-touched surface in any home. QT4+: brackets removed for horizontal painting. QT5: feel test + optional poly topcoat.

paintable_items.name: Stair Base Rail (Shoe Rail)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Linear feet of base rail to be repainted. Conditional -- not all railing systems have base rails. 3 accessible surfaces.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC. Conditional item. When present, runs parallel to handrail at tread level.

variants.notes: BASELINE. Most common residential stair repaint. Sound paint, degloss + 2 finish coats, no prime. Brush application in occupied home.
Standard RP on failing paint. Scrape/feather + state-driven prime + 2 finish coats. Common on high-wear stair surfaces.
Full remediation. Heavy scrape, contamination treatment, state-driven prime + 2 finish coats. Highest prep labor.
Premium refresh on sound paint. Full sand 220 between coats, systematic inspection, bracket removal. No prime needed.
Premium remediation. Full prep + state-driven prime + 2 finish coats + bracket removal.
Production spray on sound paint. HVLP preferred. Requires spray containment setup (45+ min). Break-even at 20-25 balusters.
Premium remediation spray. Full prep + state-driven prime + 2 spray finish coats. Production method for large baluster counts.
Superior refresh. 3 brush finish coats per FFD 15.10.3, thorough 220-320 interstage, bracket removal, feel test, optional poly topcoat.
Maximum effort. Full remediation + state-driven prime + 3 brush finish coats. Near-worst-case labor scenario. Gallery-quality finish.
Standard remediation spray. Scrape/feather + prime + 2 spray coats. Production method with containment.

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: Water-based adhesion promoter. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings. Critical for stairs historically painted with alkyd enamel.

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac)
material_systems_summary.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker (BIN or equivalent). Only product that seals nicotine/smoke. Full surface application required.

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: Mildew-resistant stain-blocking primer. Applied after biocide treatment. Rare on stairs but applicable for basement stairwells.

material_systems_summary.name: Fine-Finish Standard Acrylic (QT3)
material_systems_summary.notes: Standard acrylic enamel for residential stair repaint. Self-leveling, low VOC.

material_systems_summary.name: Fine-Finish Modified Urethane (QT4)
material_systems_summary.notes: Modified urethane enamel. Higher film build, better flow/leveling, increased hardness. Superior scuff resistance for high-traffic stairs.

material_systems_summary.name: Fine-Finish Premium (QT5)
material_systems_summary.notes: Premium waterborne enamel. Maximum film build, superior self-leveling, maximum hardness. 3 brush coats per FFD 15.10.3.

material_systems_summary.name: Polyurethane Topcoat for Handrails (QT5 Optional)
material_systems_summary.notes: Optional water-based polyurethane clear coat over cured enamel on handrails only. Maximum hand-oil resistance. Allow 24-48 hr enamel cure before application.

module_summary.description: Tread protection (FIRST), floor protection (landings), wall masking (spray), spray containment (balusters), carpet runner protection, safety signage, bracket removal (QT4+)
Condition scan all components, adhesion test (ASTM D3359), coating ID (latex vs oil), anti-slip verification
Lead test, containment setup, HEPA vacuum, containment removal, waste disposal (conditional: pre-1978)
TSP wash, mildew treatment, degloss per component (6 items), scrape/feather riser/stringer + railing, caulk assess/replace (3 joints), dust removal
State-driven primer per component (6 items) + sand primer + spot prime repairs
Clean area, inspect coat, sand between coats, patch defects, spot coat, tack clean, tread protect verify (runs after each coat except final)
Brush/spray finish per component (6 items x 2 methods = 12 tasks)
Final inspect, touch-up, feel test (QT5), poly topcoat (QT5), bracket reinstall (QT4+), teardown (spray/wall/carpet/floor/tread), customer walkthrough, tool cleanup

stacking_partition.prep_pool: condition_scale x component_modifier (baluster_profile OR stringer_type+access). Max realistic: 3.64x
stacking_partition.never_cross: Prep pool never includes QT. Coating pool never includes condition_scale. Contamination drives task activation, not rate modification.

protection_zones_required.notes: Ram Board Stair Armor -- FIRST task, mandatory at all tiers. NEVER plastic sheeting (fall hazard). Daily verification in RP occupied context. Removal is LAST task and may defer if tread work follows.
Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas. RP always has finished floors.
Wall masking along stringer edge and railing area. RP walls are always finished -- protection required.
Cardboard shields behind balusters, Tape & Drape on walls. HVLP preferred. 45+ min setup for typical system.
RP-specific. Rosin paper over carpet edges at paint work zones. Low-tack tape to avoid carpet backing damage.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Treads are floor-rated coating -- different system. Protection only, no edge painting. Treads painted absolutely last per doctrine.
Stringer meets wall at full length. RP walls always finished -- masking required. Caulk assess/replace at junction.
Stringer connects to baseboard at landing. Same finish group. Landing baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_INT_RP.

valid_input_states.notes: All 5 SS_INT_* states accepted. Each drives distinct prep pathway and primer selection. Different components may have different states -- handrails (high wear) may be failing while risers (low touch) remain sound. Worst state drives condition_scale.

output_state.notes: All input states normalize to SS_PAINTED_* after proper prep and coating. Semi-gloss is default stair sheen.

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: RP walls are always finished. Masking required for spray method.
Treads always protected regardless of state. Ram Board Stair Armor mandatory.

site_condition_rules.affects: safety signage, tread protection verification, customer walkthrough
site_condition_rules.notes: RP stairs are always in occupied homes. Additional safety considerations because stairs are primary circulation path.
Pre-1978 + lead-positive activates MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT. Stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint.
Contamination type drives TSP wash activation and biocide treatment.
RP-specific. Occupied homes may have carpet runner on stairs.

cross_spec_coordination.deduplication_note: MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT is shared across all interior RP specs -- do not duplicate lead-safe tasks when running stair RP alongside wall RP or trim RP.
cross_spec_coordination.shared_session_note: Stair RP typically runs alongside SF_TRIM_INT_RP (landing baseboard). Tread protection from stair spec covers landing area that trim spec would also protect. Coordinate to avoid duplicate protection. If tread work (SF_STAIR_TREAD spec) follows, defer tread protection removal.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup (tread protect FIRST, floor protect, wall mask, spray contain, carpet protect, signage, bracket remove) -> Assess (condition/adhesion/coating ID/anti-slip) -> RRP (if pre-1978) -> Prep (TSP, mildew, degloss per component canonical, scrape/feather, caulk assess, dust removal) -> Prime (state-driven per component canonical, sand primer, spot prime) -> Interstage -> Finish 1 -> Interstage -> Finish 2 (QT3+) -> [QT5 brush: Interstage -> Finish 3] -> Final Inspect -> Touch-up -> Feel Test (QT5) -> Poly Topcoat (QT5) -> Bracket Reinstall (QT4+) -> Teardown -> Customer Walkthrough -> Tool Cleanup
sequencing_notes.canonical_sequence: Within every coat module: stringers (#4) -> risers (#8) -> balusters (#5) -> newels (#6) -> handrails (#7) -> base rails
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO painting over active moisture. NO latex primer on smoke damage (shellac only). NO plastic sheeting on treads (fall hazard). NO skipping interstage sanding on stairs -- all tiers. Spot prime ALL scraped/repaired areas.
sequencing_notes.tread_protection_note: Tread protection is FIRST task and LAST removal. Daily verification in occupied home context. May defer removal if tread work follows.

relationships.notes: Sixth interior RP spec. Consolidates two NC specs (riser + railing) into single RP spec. NC specs are siblings with significant task adaptation. Context prefix STRP avoids collision with NC prefixes STRS (riser) and STRL (railing).

sections_used: Shellac stain-blocker mandate for smoke damage (RC-002)

change_log.author: SpecFactory Assembly Agent
change_log.changes: Initial spec.json assembly from 5 pipeline artifacts (research, resolution, materials, sop_modules, production). QA Critic found 1 major issue (task count summary off by 1) -- fixed in sop_modules.json and production.json. pass_with_warnings. 69 tasks across 8 modules (7 owned MOD_STRP_* + 1 shared MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT), 7 material systems (3 state-driven primers + 3 QT-driven fine-finish + 1 optional poly topcoat), 4 round configurations, 5 protection zones, 3 adjacent surfaces, 15 PaintScope inputs, 10 variants, 6 paintable items with dual UOM (EA + LF). Consolidates SF_STAIR_RISER_NC (30 tasks) + SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC (43 tasks) = 73 NC tasks into 69 RP tasks. Context prefix STRP. Sixth interior RP spec.
